headline: Foreign money pours back as Mahanadi Coalfields prices its big IPO

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Monday, the sixteenth of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most this morning. First, foreign money is pouring back. Foreign portfolio investors put around 84,290 crore rupees into Indian shares in just nine sessions this month, after pulling money out in September and October.

Second, the biggest public issue of the season now has a price. Coal India's arm Mahanadi Coalfields will sell shares at 129 to 136 rupees each when its offer opens on Thursday.

And third, the rate worry is growing. With inflation above 6 percent and oil near 95 dollars, economists now expect the Reserve Bank to raise rates further. And a big week for global technology lies ahead, with Nvidia's results due on Tuesday.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed. On Friday, the Nifty fell 0.6 percent to end at 25,144, as the inflation number rattled traders. Even so, it was the Nifty's third straight weekly gain, its first such streak since June. Mid and small caps did better than the leaders, and public sector banks and oil and gas stocks were among the gainers.

The flows tell the story. Foreign institutional investors bought about 5,737 crore rupees of shares on Friday alone, while domestic institutions sold about 2,254 crore rupees, using the rally to book profits. From the second to the thirteenth of November, foreign investors put in 84,290 crore rupees, after taking out about 34,843 crore in October and 35,861 crore in September. That has cut their net selling for the year to about 2.1 lakh crore rupees. Financials, telecom, capital goods, pharma and autos drew the most buying. A report carried by Moneycontrol says the MSCI India index has bounced 11 percent from its October low, as India's limited exposure to artificial intelligence turns into an advantage while money rotates out of the crowded AI trade.

Not everyone is convinced. Sundaram's Anand Radhakrishnan says it is too early to call this a trend, and points to cheaper crude, a steadier rupee and better earnings as more lasting reasons than the AI retreat. Jefferies' Christopher Wood sees a fresh escalation involving Iran as the biggest risk for Indian shares.

This morning, the market opened firmer. In early trade, the Nifty was above 25,200 and the Sensex was up about 380 points, with Eicher Motors up 3 percent and Kaynes Technology down 10 percent. For the levels, Moneycontrol's analysts see support at 25,000 and then 24,800, with resistance at 25,200 to 25,300, and then 25,424 as the crucial hurdle.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to IPOs and deals. The primary market is back, with three issues worth over 10,000 crore rupees opening this week.

The headliner is Mahanadi Coalfields, Coal India's largest coal-producing subsidiary. The price band is 129 to 136 rupees a share. After the employee discount, the issue raises about 8,981 crore rupees, and values the company at about 90,010 crore rupees at the top of the band. It is a pure offer for sale, with Coal India selling 66.18 crore shares, or 10 percent of the company, so the money goes to Coal India, not to Mahanadi. The issue is open from Thursday, the nineteenth, to Monday, the twenty-third, and the shares are tentatively due to list on the twenty-seventh.

Before that, Crystal Crop Protection opens on Wednesday, the eighteenth, and closes on the twentieth. It is raising about 455 crore rupees at 259 to 272 rupees a share. Livemint reports a grey market premium of 14 rupees, pointing to a listing gain of around 5 percent. On the small-company platform, Watrana Rentals opens on the nineteenth with a 120 crore rupee issue, priced at 232 to 245 rupees, in lots of 600 shares.

One banking matter to note. A contempt petition by Axis Trustee Services against Yes Bank has brought back the Supreme Court ruling on its written-off additional tier one bonds, with a potential bill of around 8,400 crore rupees for the bank.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
A short results roundup, as the September quarter season winds down.

In autos, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Eicher Motors, Ashok Leyland and Hero Motors are all in focus after their numbers, and Eicher rose about 3 percent in early trade. Electronics maker Kaynes Technology fell about 10 percent at the open after its results.

In capital goods, ABB India has reported, while Hitachi Energy's shares have soared on strong earnings, big order inflows and its confidence in upcoming high voltage transmission projects. More broadly, a Moneycontrol analysis finds that global headwinds squeezed capital goods margins, with resilient demand at home only partly making up for it.

In retail, Baazar Style Retail said revenue from operations fell from a year ago, to about 478 crore rupees, though the stock had gained about 20 percent in the week before the results. Godrej Industries and Zetwerk are among the other names in focus.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy and policy.

The Reserve Bank's next move is the big question. Retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent in October, the ninth straight monthly rise, with food inflation near 9 percent. Business Standard reports that economists and traders now expect the Reserve Bank to raise its benchmark rate by another 50 to 75 basis points in the coming months, which would take it as high as 6.25 percent, from 5.5 percent now. Price pressure is also spreading. Mobile phone prices rose 8.65 percent in October, and a Moneycontrol analysis finds 95 of 358 items in the basket running above 6 percent. Wholesale inflation for October is due today.

On trade, October brought a record and a worry. Exports jumped 45 percent to a record 49.47 billion dollars, led by petroleum, electronics, engineering goods, and gems and jewellery. But imports rose 16 percent to 89.35 billion dollars, so the trade deficit widened to a one-year high of 39.88 billion dollars.

On growth, SBI Research expects the economy to have grown 7.8 percent in the September quarter, above the Reserve Bank's estimate of 7.2 percent.

A few policy notes. Reserve Bank deputy governor Murmu said the central bank is unlikely to ease the 50 percent cap on how much of a borrower's income can go to microfinance repayments. The production linked incentive schemes have created 8.49 lakh jobs, just 28 percent of their target, and the government is looking at tweaks. Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator will soon issue rules for using artificial intelligence in the markets, built around disclosure, accountability and human oversight. And ahead of the Budget, industry bodies are asking for cuts to long-term capital gains tax.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, all eyes are on technology this week. Nvidia reports on Tuesday, a week after news of an affair involving chief executive Jensen Huang cut its market value by about 2 trillion dollars. Anthropic's IPO is also set to test the market. On Friday, the Nasdaq fell 0.9 percent as chip stocks came under pressure, and this morning Japan's Nikkei is down 0.6 percent.

In America, a hotter than expected wholesale inflation reading has strengthened bets on a quarter point Federal Reserve rate hike in December. The 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.14 percent, and the dollar index is at a 19-month high. The minutes of the Fed's last meeting and American retail sales are due this week.

On oil, Brent is around 95 dollars a barrel, a little lower this morning, as the International Energy Agency flags a growing global surplus. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see Brent testing 90 to 92 dollars, though fresh incidents in the Strait of Hormuz keep the risk alive.

Gold edged higher this morning as traders await remarks from Warsh at the Fed, after gold and silver lost over 4 percent last week. And Bitcoin slid to a three-month low of about 63,300 dollars as forced selling picked up.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money.

Two tax rulings worth knowing. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted a 1.5 crore rupee addition against an advertising firm that the department had built on a WhatsApp chat and a photo of a 10 rupee note. The tribunal held that third-party messages and statements did not prove the company was part of the alleged cash deal. And the Mumbai bench allowed a deduction of 2.51 crore rupees under section 54F to a taxpayer who sold six commercial units and bought two flats on different floors.

The Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court held that a pension cannot be attached to recover someone else's loan, even when the retired employee stood guarantor. And a Delhi consumer commission ordered a bank to refund 70,084 rupees lost in unauthorised online transactions, plus 25,000 rupees in compensation and costs.

On deposits, Indian Overseas Bank raised its 444-day rate by up to 15 basis points, to 6.85 percent, and some small finance banks are offering up to 8.25 percent. Gold has fallen sharply at home, by over 6,600 rupees in three days in Meerut, to below 1.36 lakh rupees, just as the wedding season begins.

A warning from SBI: fraudsters are calling about electricity bills, asking for KYC updates and sending payment links. The bank says not to fall for them. And bank branches in Patna and Ranchi are shut today for Chhath Puja.

That's your brief. Today, watch October's wholesale inflation, whether the foreign buying keeps going, and how the Nifty handles the 25,300 mark. Later in the week come Nvidia's results on Tuesday, the Fed minutes, and Mahanadi Coalfields opening on Thursday. Have a good Monday.
